title: The evaluation harness
question: Chunk size or encoder: which lever matters?
finding_html: The encoder. bge-small over minilm bought +0.128 MRR (0.627 → 0.754) at zero extra cost. Halving the chunk size hurt both encoders. At n=20 one question is worth 0.05 MRR, so the encoder gain clears the noise floor and the 0.015 gaps do not.
metric_label: MRR from the encoder swap, at n=20; the n=50 re-run gives +0.037

title: Reading the chunks by hand
question: Where does the keyword ruler disagree with a human?
finding_html: On the question I had already written off. Reading the retrieved text overturned my own earlier verdict and reclassified the miss from a coverage problem to a ranking problem, which is what pointed experiment 06 at a cross encoder.

title: Heading aware chunking
question: Does splitting on headings rescue a known miss?
finding_html: No. The target chunk fell from full corpus rank #8 to #67. Cleaner chunks helped it, and helped 66 competitors more. Aggregate MRR rose 0.013 while the question I was fixing went backwards, which is the argument for per-question diffs.
metric_label: target chunk rank after the change

title: Retrieve wide, then rerank
question: Can a cross encoder rescue the two misses?
finding_html: One of two. LSTM flipped to a hit at pool 20. Overfitting stayed a miss at every pool size from 5 to 30, scoring −9.01, so being in the pool was necessary and not sufficient. A scoring decision, not a recall problem.

title: What an answer costs
question: Cost, latency, and what new failure mode did I buy?
finding_html: $0.002174 per query, 2.1 s mean latency, input 59% of the bill. A live price check overruled my own memory, which had the model down as fiction. And a probe returned "Paris, the capital of France" from context that never mentioned it.

title: RAG, fine-tune, or prompt
question: Which tool fits which problem, with a number?
finding_html: Four scenarios sorted on knowledge versus behaviour, with the break-even written out: ~$72.47/day saved means a small-model fine-tune pays back in days. Stability lets a one-time cost amortise; churn kills it.
metric_label: break-even that pays for a fine-tune

title: Closing the hallucination gap
question: Will it answer questions the corpus cannot support?
finding_html: The prompt I had been shipping hallucinated on 15 of 15 trap runs. Not a flicker, a flatline. A better prompt alone took it to 0 of 15, faithfulness 3.90 → 4.80, groundedness 66.9% → 95.6%. Plus a CI gate that exits non-zero.

title: Abstention in production telemetry
question: There is no test set in production. How would I know?
finding_html: A boolean score on every span. Traps 5/5, golden 1/20. The one false abstention traced to one chunk in 734, so a chunking defect rather than a timid model. Band set at 0 < rate ≤ 0.10, because never abstaining is the failure of experiment 09.
metric_label: chunk behind the one false abstention

title: Is a search loop worth it?
question: Does letting the model search again fix anything?
finding_html: Four of five preregistered hypotheses were wrong. The loop closed a defect that had survived five experiments, 3/3 at 5/5 faithfulness. It fired on 2 questions in 20, zero false fires, 1.32× cost. Ship behind a trigger, not by default.

title: The attack that scores grounded
question: What if someone can write into my corpus?
finding_html: 1,820 bytes, 0.255% of the corpus, obeyed 8 of 18 runs. My own faithfulness judge scored the most successful attack 5/5, fully grounded, 3/3. A nonce delimiter cut obedience to 1/18 at zero quality cost and 1.68× money. The injection that issues no order still walks through.
metric_label: runs obeyed, cut to 1 of 18 by a nonce

title: The stage that cannot be argued with
question: Does forcing citations stop the attack?
finding_html: No. It catches none of the eight attacks that landed, because the attacker's method is to make the citation true. Segregating the judge did work: correct answers wrongly punished went 4 to 0. And my own validator blocked two correct answers, from a prose contract with two readings.

title: Serving the retriever over MCP
question: Can I expose my index as an MCP server?
finding_html: Built to the 2026-07-28 spec and verified three ways, including Claude Code discovering and calling it unprompted. A poisoned tool description got 0/3 compliance but 1/3 contamination: the model reasoned about a tool it never called.

title: Kill it, then resume it
question: Does LangGraph durability survive a crash?
finding_html: Only on a flag that is not the default. With durability="async", a kill -9 lost a model call I had already paid for. sync fixes it. Verdict: keep my own loop, and the condition that would change that is written down.
metric_label: paid for and lost on kill -9 with async
